chunks: Ali ibn al-Nu'man narrated from Ibn Muskān, from Dāwūd, from Abū Shaybah al-Zuhrī, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him) who said:

The worst servant is he who is of two faces and two tongues, who compliments his brother in his presence and devours him in his absence; when he is given, he envies him, and when he is wronged, he abandons him.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of a hypocritical person in Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) characterizes the 'two-faced' servant as one whose outward praise masks inner envy and whose loyalty is transactional, abandoning the oppressed while envying the generous. In Shia scholarly tradition, this serves as a critical warning against *riya* (showing off) and *ghibah* (backbiting), highlighting how hypocrisy corrupts social bonds by turning relationships into conditional exchanges rather than acts of genuine brotherhood. The description of 'eating' the brother in his absence vividly illustrates the destructive nature of slander, which consumes the victim's reputation just as one consumes food.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 5.ʿAlī ibn al-Nuʿmān narrated from Ibn Muskān, from Dāwūd, from Abū Shaybah al-Zuhrī, from one of the two (Imam al-Bāqir or al-Ṣādiq) (a) who said, “

The worst servant [of Allah] is he who possesses a doubleface and a forked-tongue, he compliments his brother in his presence yet backbites him in his absence. When he is given, he envies him and when he is wronged, he abandons him.”
